translation: I have heard that in the age of high antiquity, formulas were not equal to physicians; in the age of middle antiquity, physicians were not equal to formulas, greatly. How medicine and formulas are both valued! As the age declined, the formulas became ever more mixed and disorderly; each relied on the words of one school, mutually affirming and denying each other. Occasionally there were two or three proven formulas, but they were only transmitted by fathers and teachers to their sons and disciples, and never lightly shown to others. And those that were carved and circulated in the world were mostly copies of the same gourd, sometimes changing the head and face to win a high reputation, and that was all.
